headline: Uncertainty and verified metrics probe reliability of AI-guided drug discovery
label: Trustworthy Ai For Discovery
summary: Recent preprints test whether AI-guided screening, retrieval and data extraction yield calibrated, budget-aware or proteome-scale predictions.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the reliability of AI-driven decisions in drug and molecular discovery, where outputs are judged by explicit evaluation criteria, coverage or scale rather than point accuracy alone. BSDS/DQS formalizes budget-aware scoring of AI selection with Lean 4 verification and reports that LLMs add no value over random forest on MoleculeNet HIV data. Conformal prediction applied to candidate-based retrieval from LC-MS/MS spectra yields spectrum-specific prediction sets with target coverage. HARVEST uses multi-agent LLMs to extract 3.15M bioactivity records from 164,877 USPTO patents and introduces H-Bench. OmniBind targets proteome-wide promiscuity prediction for early-stage screening, where off-target binding is a leading cause of attrition. Only the retrieval paper explicitly attaches coverage guarantees to its outputs; the remaining items address evaluation, data extraction and off-target scale.
